To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the western Moravian crystalline complex is composed of blocks of various size, separated by faults and shear zones; that these faults and shear zones are of various origin, some are inherited, some are of late Hercynian age; that the late Hercynian shear zones are characterized by statistically isotropic orientation of quartz; and that the orientation of quartz is not a result of deformation alone, but it is also controlled by chemical composition of the rock.
The quartz fabrics in the crystalline basement of Western Moravia are statistically isotropic.
